question.prompt: A high-speed railway line is 780 km long. If the average speed increases from 260 km/h to 312 km/h, by how many hours does the total travel time decrease? (You may give a decimal.)

solutions.explanation: The original travel time is \(780\div260=3\) h. After the speed increase, it is \(780\div312=2.5\) h. The decrease is \(3-2.5=0.5\) h.
solutions.title: Calculate and subtract the travel times
